revisit_notes: eta_gg (GG secular-desaturation efficiency) is a modeled band [0.15,0.5], NOT derived from a control law; H1 clear-time inherits that uncertainty. The falsify line (30 d) clears even at eta=0.15.

GG desaturates in-orbit-plane momentum only; the component along the orbit normal still needs a small thruster/RW trim. Leg B is 'mostly plume-free', not strictly zero-fire. Quantifying the residual-axis fraction is a named follow-on.
Thruster propellant is despin's 125 kg/15000 N.m.s scaled linearly (angular impulse is linear in L at fixed geometry) — consistent, not a new derivation. Leg A's cost claim rests on despin, not here.
CMG mass anchored to ISS M2000 (272 kg/4760 N.m.s). Even the lightest flown CMG keeps buffer mass an order above the ~42 kg propellant, so H2's direction is anchor-robust.

verdict.summary: GG-desat is real and boulder-strengthened (clears a berth in 2.5-10 d) but NOT free: it costs ~300-600 kg CMG buffer + a days-scale berth-cadence floor, vs ~42 kg water propellant for a thruster dump. Capture-geometry control (leg C) eliminates the dump entirely where v_c*r_off<=0.0075 m^2/s is reachable and is the preferred architecture; leg A (cheap thrusters, manage plume) is the robust fallback; leg B (GG-desat) is reserved for the case where plume at the bag is a hard showstopper.
